channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Apoiadores de Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro fazem últimos atos de campanha em Apucarana
item.description: Supporters of Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro held their final campaign rallies in Apucarana, reinforcing positions ahead of the runoff. The events gathered sympathizers from both sides for closing speeches before the election.

item.title: Esquerda mobiliza hashtag em apoio a Lula após Flávio chamá-lo de nove dedos em debate
item.description: After Flávio Bolsonaro called Lula 'nine fingers' during a debate, the left-wing mobilized the hashtag #SomosTodosNoveDedos in support of the president, posting criticisms of the opponent's statement on social media.

item.title: CNT/MDA: Flávio tem 50,7% dos votos válidos e Lula, 49,3%; mulheres são maioria entre indecisos
item.description: The CNT/MDA poll shows Flávio Bolsonaro leading with 50.7% and Lula with 49.3% in the second round, within technical tie. Women account for 4% of undecided voters, compared to 1% of men.

item.title: Manifestantes se reúnem em ato em apoio a Flávio Bolsonaro em BH
item.description: Supporters of Flávio Bolsonaro held a rally at Praça da Liberdade in Belo Horizonte during the final rally before the presidential runoff. The event gathered protesters supporting the Rio senator's campaign for president.

item.title: Mesmo com desculpas de Flávio, PL mantém nas redes fala sobre nove dedos
item.description: The PL party reposted on social media a joke by Flávio Bolsonaro about Lula's physical disability, despite the senator apologizing to the president during the TV Globo debate. The move sparked criticism for maintaining an offensive discourse despite the conciliatory gesture. The episode highlights polarization and the use of controversial humor in the 2026 election campaign.

item.title: Médico do Einstein diz ter recursos para não atender 'petista vagabundo'
item.description: Dr. Clederson Henry Dina from the Albert Einstein Hospital faced backlash after making derogatory remarks against supporters of President Lula, including stating he has "resources" to not treat "vagabond PT supporters". The comments sparked controversy on social media.

item.title: MPE pede anulação da candidatura de Canella por ligação com milícias
item.description: The MPE requested the TSE to annul Márcio Canella's candidacy (União Brasil) due to alleged ties with militias and the Comando Vermelho. The filed opinion states there are indications of the politician's involvement with criminal organizations. TSE's decision on the case is still pending.

item.title: PT diz que Metrô recuou sobre instalação de tapumes no entorno de estações
item.description: The São Paulo Metro retracted permission for campaign-installed barriers around Trianon-Masp and Consolação stations, requesting their removal overnight on Saturday, October 24, before Lula's final campaign rally on Paulista Avenue. Lula's campaign had coordinated the barriers with the company to protect public infrastructure from vandalism. The incident follows the Metro filing a police report for damage to stations after a previous rally.

item.title: Em BH, Flávio se abraça em deputada que recebia mesada na Farra do INSS
item.description: In Belo Horizonte, Senator Flávio Bolsonaro was photographed embracing state deputy Chiara Biondini, who is under investigation for receiving R$ 60,000 from Conafer in an INSS fraud scheme. The deputy, daughter of federal deputy Eros Biondini, was allegedly used to pressure her father politically. The image sparked backlash for linking Flávio to figures involved in corruption schemes.

item.title: Elecciones en Brasil, en vivo | Bolsonaro y Lula apuran la campaña con dos actos en dos ciudades cada uno
item.description: The 2026 Brazilian presidential race is tied between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, with heated debates on security and economy. The outcome will resonate across Latin America, influencing the region's rightward shift.

item.title: Colunistas do Metrópoles analisam quem venceu debate da Globo; veja notas
item.description: Metrópoles columnists assessed the TV Globo debate between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, giving each candidate a score of 5. The debate highlighted economic proposals, with criticisms of policy copying and discussions on public debt and food prices.

item.title: Lula convoca “exército” para buscar quem não votou no 1º turno
item.description: Lula rallied supporters in Copacabana to encourage non-voters from the first round to head to the polls in the runoff. He emphasized voting as essential to strengthening Brazilian democracy and criticized Flávio Bolsonaro’s proposals, such as SUS privatization. The event featured allied politicians and public figures from Rio de Janeiro.

item.title: Pneu de carro fura em ato no Rio, e Lula aproveita contratempo para alfinetar Flávio: 'Ele diria que iria voando'
item.description: While campaigning in Rio de Janeiro, President Lula had a tire blowout on his pickup truck and used the setback to mock rival Flávio Bolsonaro, claiming he would have lied about it. Lula emphasized the importance of voting to strengthen democracy and referenced the case of 5-year-old Ana Clara, killed by a police bullet.

item.title: Lula diz estar confiante de que vencerá eleição porque 'brasileiros não podem levar um miliciano para o Palácio do Planalto'
item.description: President Lula expressed confidence in winning the election, arguing that Brazilians should not elect a militia member to the Presidential Palace. He emphasized the threat to democracy, freedom, and the well-being of society. Lula predicted his re-election in the runoff.

item.title: Lula chama Flávio de ‘candidato de baixo nível’ e volta a rebater ataque capacitista
item.description: Lula called Flávio 'the lowest-level candidate' and linked him to militias during a campaign rally in Rio. Recalling the Globo debate, the president accused his rival of dishonesty and highlighted the legal dispute over the Ilha Comprida land involving Richarlison, allegedly favored by SPU processing granted to his ally Willer Tomaz.

item.title: Florianópolis, Goiânia, Aracaju: atos de Lula e Flávio mobilizam apoiadores pelo país; veja vídeos
item.description: Lula and Flávio mobilize supporters in simultaneous acts across multiple cities the day before the second round. Events take place in Florianópolis, Goiânia, Aracaju, Maceió and Fortaleza, with videos going viral on social media.

item.title: Menção ao caso Ana Clara e atuação de Flávio Bolsonaro: ONU analisa denúncia sobre milícias no Rio em dezembro
item.description: The UN will review a complaint in December regarding the expansion of militias in Rio de Janeiro, including the case of the girl Ana Clara. The complaint alleges suspected connections between criminal groups and public officials, citing figures such as Flávio Bolsonaro, Jair Bolsonaro, and Cláudio Castro.

item.title: Ao vivo: Flávio realiza ato na Barra da Tijuca
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) holds a campaign rally in Barra da Tijuca, Rio de Janeiro, starting at 2 PM on Saturday (Oct 24, 2026), after spending time in Belo Horizonte. Rio de Janeiro, Minas Gerais, and São Paulo are strategic states in the final stretch of the campaign, home to the largest number of voters in the country. In Minas Gerais, historically, 95% of presidents elected since 1945 have won there, highlighting its decisive role.

item.title: Gênero e religião: como Flávio e Lula lidaram com eleitores que mais os rejeitam
item.description: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro's campaigns attempt to mitigate rejection among vulnerable demographics, with Lula reaching out to evangelical voters and Flávio addressing criticism from women, though neither has reversed underlying rejection trends.

item.title: Desafio de Lula é convencer de que será diferente; o de Flávio é mostrar que não será um Bukele
item.description: In the Brazilian runoff election, Lula and Flávio converge on some proposals but diverge sharply on public security: Flávio supports greater military involvement and joining the Shield of the Americas, while Lula prefers keeping Brazil out of it and creating a Ministry of Public Security to coordinate anti-crime efforts.

item.title: Por que duelo entre Lula e Flávio é crucial para a América Latina — e para Trump
item.description: The runoff between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro is crucial for Latin America and the U.S., influencing regional dynamics and international relations. Flávio advocates for economic liberalism and strict security, while Lula promotes state expansion and social policies. The election also reflects tensions over Jair Bolsonaro's legacy and continental polarization.

item.title: Ato de Flávio Bolsonaro em BH tem criança com farda e fuzil de brinquedo
item.description: During a campaign rally in Belo Horizonte, a child dressed in military uniform and holding a toy rifle attracted the attention of supporters of Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). The child, accompanied by his father, made the V-sign as Bolsonaro's motorcade passed through Praça da Liberdade. The event took place after the presidential debate between Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL).

item.title: TSE verifica urnas para eleição e emite relatório de segurança para totalização de votos no segundo turno
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court verified the electronic systems used in the elections and issued the 'zeroth of the count', ensuring no pre-computed votes for the runoff candidates. The procedure confirms the readiness and integrity of the vote transmission and counting systems.

item.title: Pesquisa Colectta mostra Lula com 50,3%, contra 49,7% de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: A poll by Instituto Colectta, released on October 24, 2026, shows Lula (PT) with 50.3% of valid votes and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) with 49.7%, indicating a technical tie. The survey was based on 3,000 in-person interviews conducted across 101 cities, with a margin of error of two percentage points and a 95% confidence level. When considering total votes, Lula leads with 46.5% against Flávio's 46%, while 4.4% indicate blank or null votes.

item.title: La rebelión en la calle y un ejército digital impulsan a Lula
item.description: Lula enters the runoff with renewed strength, backed by street movements and a digital army challenging Meta's algorithms, particularly against Flávio Bolsonaro's far-right agenda. His initially lukewarm campaign and first-round loss were overturned through popular mobilization and aggressive digital strategies.

item.title: Flávio assina petição para rever condenação de Filipe Martins
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) signed a petition to the IACHR requesting the revision of Filipe Martins' conviction, a former Jair Bolsonaro aide sentenced for involvement in the coup plot. The document was filed by Flávio and other lawyers, according to Folha.

item.title: Lula diz em Copacabana que “arma” é a urna e “bala” é o 13
item.description: During a campaign rally in Copacabana, Lula stated that the ballot box is his 'weapon' and the number 13 of the PT is his 'ammunition,' reinforcing support for reelection against Flávio Bolsonaro. He also publicly criticized Flávio, calling him a 'militiaman' and accusing him of intending to privatize the SUS and abolish the 6 X 1 shift schedule.

item.title: Debate da Globo movimenta 33,7 milhões de menções nas redes em menos de 12 horas: veja quem ganhou
item.description: The Globo presidential debate generated 33.7 million social media mentions in under 12 hours, with 56.4% favoring Lula and 43.6% favoring Flávio Bolsonaro. Lula led in volume and engagement, while Flávio stood out in efficiency, proportional follower growth, and most-viewed video. Topics such as security, health, pandemic memory, and debate winner claims shaped the discussion.

item.title: O voto que neutraliza o voto: efeito mobilização ou efeito rebote? Leia artigo de Felipe Nunes, diretor da Quaest
item.description: The article examines the voter participation paradox and the impact of mobilization in 2026 elections, noting that 21.07% abstention in the first round favors Lula, but the bounce effect may benefit Flávio if his base also mobilizes to neutralize opposing votes.

item.title: Lula chama Flávio Bolsonaro de candidato de ‘mais baixo nível’ durante ato no Rio
item.description: At a campaign rally in Copacabana, Lula criticized Flávio Bolsonaro, calling him the lowest-level candidate he has faced and linking him to militias, warning of risks to democracy. The event brought together supporters in intense heat, with some needing medical care. Lula then headed to São Paulo for another walk and will vote in the runoff.

item.title: Toffoli defende regras para que campanhas não usem canais e propaganda como 'ringue'
item.description: TSE minister Dias Toffoli advocated for the creation of rules to prevent election campaigns from turning communication channels and political advertisements into a 'ring'. His proposal aims to foster a more professional and respectful debate during elections. The statement was made on the eve of the 2026 runoff election.

item.title: Disputa do 2º turno: Como acompanhar os resultados das eleições 2026 em tempo real
item.description: The Estadão will broadcast real-time results of the 2026 second-round elections, with vote counting starting after polls close at 5 PM. The race features Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) versus Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), along with gubernatorial contests in five states and the Federal District.

item.title: Procurador eleitoral vê ligação de Canella com Comando Vermelho e pede a TSE que derrube candidatura
item.description: Deputy Attorney General Alexandre Espinosa requested that the TSE block the candidacy of Márcio Canella, elected state representative for União Brasil in Rio de Janeiro, due to alleged ties with the Comando Vermelho and involvement in a money laundering scheme. Canella was arrested in the eighth phase of the Federal Police's Operation Unha e Carne.

item.title: Prioridade para conclusão da Transnordestina é consenso de Lula e Flávio
item.description: Lula and Flávio reached a consensus on prioritizing the completion of the Transnordestina Railway in the next government, regardless of the election outcome. The project, over 20 years in progress with delays, covers 1,206 km at a cost of BRL 15 billion, part of which has already been spent. Both candidates emphasized infrastructure's role in regional development and the flow of agricultural and mineral production.

item.title: Flávio faz dois gols contra, mas evita goleada de Lula na Globo
item.description: In a Globo debate, Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro tied at 50% in valid votes from Datafolha. Flávio scored three goals, two against, avoiding a loss for his opponent but failing to surpass Lula.

item.title: Quem é Mariana? Janones associa exploração de mulheres a aliados de Flávio
item.description: Federal deputy André Janones (Rede-MG) associated Mariana Vishegirskaya, a Ukrainian woman photographed during the 2022 Mariupol maternity hospital bombing, with suspicions of refugee exploitation in Brazil, indirectly linking the case to Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) and his alleged ally Daniel Vorcaro, while denying any direct connection between the young woman and the candidate. He used the case to denounce potential sexual exploitation networks targeting Ukrainian refugees and called for investigations.

item.title: Manifestantes se concentram em Copacabana para ato pró-Lula
item.description: Supporters gathered at Copacabana Beach backing Lula's re-election, where he sharply criticized Flávio Bolsonaro following the TV Globo debate. Lula accused his opponent of dishonesty and evasiveness, emphasizing the need to occupy public spaces ahead of the runoff.

item.title: Leia o que a mídia internacional diz sobre o debate da “Globo”
item.description: International media highlighted the polarized debate between Lula and Flavio Bolsonaro, especially personal provocations like the 'nine fingers' comment. Outlets emphasized disagreements on economy and corruption, while criticism of Javier Milei was also noted by Argentine press.

item.title: Vitória de Flávio seria “desastre para todo o planeta”, diz Greta
item.description: Greta Thunberg stated that a victory by Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) would be a 'disaster for the entire planet', emphasizing the impact of the Brazilian elections on the future of the Amazon and climate change. The environmental activist warned about the environmental consequences of a potential Flávio administration, particularly for the country's critical ecosystems.

item.title: Ex-ministros de Lula e Dilma declaram apoio a Flávio
item.description: Two former ministers from the Lula and Dilma governments, Aldo Rebelo and Roberto Mangabeira Unger, expressed support for Flávio Bolsonaro in the 2026 runoff during a meeting in São Paulo. The discussion covered economy, the Amazon, and foreign policy, with no mention of position bargaining. The move highlights the shifting alliances amid electoral polarization.

item.title: MP Eleitoral aponta ligação de Canella com a milícia e pede ao TSE para negar registro da candidatura
item.description: The Electoral Public Ministry has requested the TSE to reject Márcio Canella's candidacy for state deputy in Rio de Janeiro, alleging ties to militias and membership in a criminal organization. The lawmaker allegedly appointed militia leaders to positions in the city hall of Belford Roxo and is currently under investigation for organized crime.

item.title: Ao vivo: Lula participa de caminhada em Copacabana
item.description: The president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), takes part in walks in two capitals: first in Rio de Janeiro at 10am at Posto 5 in Copacabana, then along Atlântica Avenue, and afterward in São Paulo at 4pm, with a gathering in front of Masp on Paulista Avenue, heading toward Haddock Lobo street. The activity is part of a social and political mobilization agenda.

item.title: Redes bolsonaristas espalhando o medo de olho na abstenção
item.description: Bolsonarist networks spread false claim that left-wing protesters will riot if Lula loses. The disinformation aims to discourage voting. Full article available for subscribers only.

item.title: 'Lula coloca Bolsonaro na defensiva': imprensa internacional destaca 'debate crucial' da TV Globo
item.description: The debate between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro on TV Globo drew international attention, with El País claiming Lula put his opponent on the defensive. The PT candidate took a more aggressive stance, while Flávio attempted to present himself as more moderate, particularly on social policies and public security.

item.title: MP Eleitoral diz que não cabe à Justiça decidir sobre sigilos de candidatos e defende extinção do caso
item.description: The Electoral Public Ministry defended the dismissal of the case requesting the release of sigils of Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, arguing there is no strictly electoral matter involved. The deputy electoral attorney general Alexandre Espinosa stated there are no elements to justify the Electoral Justice intervention in the case.

item.title: Agenda do dia: Lula fecha campanha em São Paulo e Flávio vai ao Rio
item.description: On Saturday (October 24), Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) hold their final campaign rallies ahead of the 2026 presidential election second round. Street propaganda is allowed until 10 PM. Lula walks along Copacabana in the morning and rallies on Paulista Avenue in the afternoon, accompanied by allies such as Alckmin, Haddad, and Marina Silva. Flávio Bolsonaro campaigns in Belo Horizonte and then in Rio's Barra da Tijuca.

item.title: Eleições 2026: veja onde o transporte público será gratuito no segundo turno e quais são as regras
item.description: Over 158.7 million voters will head to the polls in the 2026 second-round elections and can use free public transport in cities like Rio de Janeiro and São Paulo, as per TSE Resolution No. 23.751/2026. While Rio offers free access to buses, metro, BRT, and VLT from 6 AM to 8 PM, São Paulo provides 24/7 free service with expanded lines. The benefit does not automatically apply to intercity or executive services.

item.title: Pazolini x Ferraço – Os números dos candidatos a governador do Espírito Santo (ES) no segundo turno das eleições 2026
item.description: Lorenzo Pazolini (Republicanos) and Ricardo Ferraço (MDB) are competing in the 2026 runoff election for governor of Espírito Santo. Pazolini leads with 49.65% of the votes in the first round; Ferraço received 34.06%. Both resigned from their positions to run for re-election.

item.title: Se vencer, Flávio Bolsonaro irá a Israel depois das eleições para pagar promessa
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro promised to travel to Israel after the election runoff to fulfill a campaign commitment. The article, labeled as subscriber-exclusive, highlights the trip as one of the candidate's pledged actions. Full content is accessible via the article link with registration.

item.title: Presidente do TSE fará pronunciamento neste sábado
item.description: The president of the TSE, Kassio Nunes Marques, will deliver a nationwide broadcast on Saturday to remind voters to confirm their polling locations before the runoff. He will also note the reduced number of venue changes compared to 2022, emphasizing that such decisions are made by electoral zones, not the TSE.
